text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Ted Kunkel, the chief executive of Australia's biggest brewer, Foster's Brewing Group, yesterday announced a 2.4 percent increase in net profit to A$169.4 million in the half-year to December and unveiled a growth strategy that involves further expansio in Asia, a doubling of earnings from wine operations, and an assault on the South American beer and wine industry. Page 1.

In a move which could considerably influence the climate for a Federal resolution to the High Court's Wik decision, negotiators hope that a deal to give the Century Zinc mining project in Queensland a green light could be signed by the seven groups of Aboriginal native title claimants on Thursday. Page 5.

Wesfarmers managing director Michael Chaney said yesterday the diversified industrial and resources group is optimistic about future growth and is poised for a sustained period of strong earnings growth and possible acquisitions after posting a 51 percent increase in half year net profit to A$57.5 million. Page 17.

Kerry Stokes's Seven Network Ltd yesterday received a conditional offer from its hostile partners in Optus Vision - Optus Communications, U.S. West and Kerry Packer's Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd - to buy 98 percent of Optus Vision for between A$534 million and A$649 million. Seven has 10 working days to accept or reject the offer. Page 17.

In a result which far exceeds mining giant WMC Ltd's original expectations, the group has received A$355 million from the sale of its U.S. oil and gas subsidiary, Greenhill Petroleum, to U.S. group Mesa Inc, with the bumper price largely due to strong oil prices. Page 17.

GE Capital Services, the Australian subsidiary of giant U.S. finance group GE Capital Corp, yesterday unveiled a A$54 million takeover offer for pallet hire group Loscam Ltd. GE Capital Services will offer Loscam shareholders 43 cents-a-share to secure 100 per cent of the company. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In the latest round of a bitter legal dispute, Optus Communications and its partners in the Optus Vision alliance - American phone giant U.S. West and Kerry Packer's Publishing & Broadcasting - are facing potentially huge losses on their investment in the venture under valuations prepared for the Seven Network Ltd's legal action against its fellow Optus Vision shareholders. Page 19.

In a move which reinforces its balance sheet ahead of its drive to join the ranks of major international mining companies, WMC has offloaded its North American oil and gas interests for A$355 million, with the proceeds to be put towards the group's multi-million-dollar plans for expansion. Page 19.

MasterCard International senior vice-president in Australia Andre Sekulic says MasterCard may sue the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games for restraint of trade in granting an exclusive licence to arch-rival Visa International or monopoly use of its cards at Games sites. Page 19.

In a surprise entry into the small business market, Australia's biggest non-bank lender, Aussie Home Loans, looks set to trigger a lending war with the introduction of a new loan set at 7.49 percent which undercuts the standard 9.75 percent rate at major banks by more than two percent. Page 19.

In a move which clears the way for Woodside Petroleum to become a major producer in the international oil market, a production licence was yesterday announced for the A$1.8 billion linked development of the Laminaria and Corallina oil fields in the Timor ea, in which Woodside is a 50 percent stakeholder and project operator. Page 21.

The northern New South Wales town of Casino is on course for a rail revival with the announcement of the Northern Rivers Railroad - a A$3 million private freight service which is the first of its type to be allowed under the Hilmer competition guidelines - which will be based in the town. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Seven Network is expected to intensify the battle with its fellow Optus Vision shareholders after yesterday revealing it had received two offers setting a price for it to acquire the 98 percent of Optus Vision now held by fellow shareholders Optus Comunications, Continental Cablevision and Publishing and Broadcasting. Page 25.

As part of a plan to sell its non-core assets to fund its ambitious A$2 billion worth of new projects and following its decision last August to quit its oil and gas portfolio, WMC has sold its oil and gas business, Greenhill Petroleum Corp, for a better-than-expected A$356 million. Page 25.

According to the head of one leading mortgage insurer, who asked not to be identified, Aussie Home Loan's foray into the small business loan market with "Aussie Business Loans", which will lend to business owners at up to 90 percent of the value of their home, Aussie may be setting itself up for a huge blow-out in dud loans. Page 25.

Satellite pay TV operator Australis Media is looking at cutting its instillation fee by half from A$200 to A$100 and reducing its monthly charge from A$49.95 to A$45 in an effort to increase its subscriber base. The price cutting plan, presented as part of a business plan to the Australis board last week by management, would make Australis more competitive against cable operators Foxtel and Optus Vision. Page 27.

Traders marked Foster's shares down 10 cents to A$2.55 yesterday despite the brewer posting A$169.4 million profit for the December half year. The price fall, which wiped almost A$200 million from Foster's market value, was attributed by one analyst to the copany not announcing a share buyback. Foster's also announced it was close to investing up to A$70 million producing beer in two new Asian markets. Page 27.

Building products and energy group Boral announced plans yesterday to increase the capacity of its Blue Circle Southern Cement works at Berrima, southern New South Wales, by about 240,000 tonnes to almost one million tonnes, costing A$33 million. The upgrade, attributed to the recovery in the construction industry, will have a positive effect for steaming coal producer Centennial Coal, which services the Berrima cement works. Page 27.
THE AGE

Australia's biggest brewer, the Foster's Brewing Group, shrugged off a 10-cent drop in its shares yesterday to A$2.55, which wiped almost A$200 million from its market value, by announcing it was close to investing up to A$70 million producing beer in two as yet unspecified, new Asian markets. Page C1.

Despite the expected release tomorrow of a sharply lower profit for the December half, WMC has received a bumper price on the sale of its Greenhill Petroleum subsidiary in the United States for A$356 million. The positive price is attributed to the surge in oil and gas asset values. Page C1.

In a further legal event in Kerry Stokes's Seven Network's march towards a court action later this month, Seven yesterday increased the pressure on its fellow Optus Vision shareholders when the Optus Vision board formally made offers to sell the rest of the company to Seven. Page C1.

Westpac, Visa International and Ansett have launched the Global Rewards Westpac Visa card to be the first co-sponsor product linked to the Sydney Olympic Games. The card has a head start in the grab for market share with Ansett's 850,000 frequent flyers. One Ansett frequent flyer point will be awarded for every dollar spent on the card. Page C3.

Satellite pay-TV operator Australis Media is aiming to be more competitive with rival cable operators Foxtel and Optus Vision by halving its installation fee and reducing its monthly charge. The price cuts are part of a plan to strengthen Australis's subcriber base and position in the industry in the event of rationalisation. Page C3.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has released draft legislation aimed at preventing trusts from passing on tax losses to third parties. The revenue saving legislation is redrafted from the former government's proposal and leaves family trusts largely untouched as long as all income distribution is kept within the family. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
